source: Payments Validator – pain.001 Validation Catalogue (Phase 1), state of 2026-11-17. Severities and reason codes are proposals until confirmed against CMIplus. Hints are drafts written for the Testing Portal.

0.1.title: The file is empty
0.1.hint: Choose the exported payment file again.

0.2.check: File size within the configured limit
0.2.title: The file is too large
0.2.hint: Split the payments into smaller files.

0.3.check: Single XML file, not an archive or other file type
0.3.title: The file is not an XML file
0.3.hint: Choose the pain.001 XML file itself, not an archive, PDF or spreadsheet.

0.5.check: Encoding is UTF-8, the declared encoding matches the bytes, no invalid byte sequences
0.5.title: The file is not UTF-8 encoded
0.5.hint: Export the file again with UTF-8 encoding.

0.7.check: Well-formed XML: one root, matching tags, escaped &, < and quotes
0.7.title: The file is not well-formed XML
0.7.hint: Correct the XML at the line shown.

0.8.check: No DOCTYPE, no external entities, entity expansion within limits (XXE protection)
0.8.title: The file contains a DOCTYPE or ENTITY declaration
0.8.hint: Remove the DOCTYPE and ENTITY declarations. Payment files must not contain them.

0.9.check: No content after the root element, such as two messages concatenated
0.9.title: There is content after the end of the message
0.9.hint: Send one message per file. Remove everything after the closing </Document> tag.

1.1.title: The root element is not Document
1.1.hint: A pain.001 file starts with the element Document.

1.2.title: The message type or version is not supported
1.2.hint: Export the file as pain.001.001.03 or pain.001.001.09.

1.3.title: The message element is not CstmrCdtTrfInitn
1.3.hint: A pain.001 Document contains the element CstmrCdtTrfInitn.

1.4.check: Detected version is accepted by CMIplus for the selected country
1.4.title: This version is not accepted for the selected country
1.4.hint: Use a pain.001 version that the bank in this country accepts.

2.1.check: Elements appear in the order the schema defines
2.1.title: Element in the wrong place
2.1.hint: Move the element to the position the ISO schema defines.

2.3.title: Element occurs too often
2.3.hint: Remove the extra occurrences of the element.

2.4.check: No unknown, misspelled or wrong-namespace elements or attributes
2.4.title: Unknown element or attribute
2.4.hint: Check the spelling and the namespace of the element, or remove it.

2.5.check: Exactly one option of each choice, e.g. IBAN or Othr, InstdAmt or EqvtAmt
2.5.title: Exactly one option of a choice is needed
2.5.hint: Give exactly one of the options the schema allows here.

2.6.check: Text within the schema length (Max35Text, Max70Text, Max140Text) and not empty
2.6.title: Text is too long or empty
2.6.hint: Shorten the text to the allowed length, or fill in the empty element.

2.7.check: Pattern types valid: BIC, IBAN, country code, currency code; in .09 also UETR and LEI
2.7.title: Value has the wrong format
2.7.hint: Correct the value to the format the schema requires (BIC, IBAN, country or currency code).

2.8.check: Schema enumerations valid: payment method, charge bearer, priority
2.8.title: Value is not one of the allowed codes
2.8.hint: Use one of the codes the schema lists.

2.9.check: Amounts: max 18 digits and 5 decimals, not negative, currency attribute present
2.9.title: Amount is not valid
2.9.hint: Write the amount with at most 18 digits and 5 decimals, not negative, with a currency.

2.10.check: Dates and date-times in ISO format
2.10.title: Date is not in ISO format
2.10.hint: Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD and date-times as YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.

2.11.title: Value must be true or false

2.x.title: Schema error
2.x.hint: Correct the element so that it matches the ISO schema.

3.1.check: Selected country has a configured rule pack
3.1.title: No country configuration for the selected country
3.1.hint: Choose one of the countries offered. If the country is offered, the bank has to add its configuration.

3.2.check: Debtor account IBAN country matches the selected country
3.2.title: Debtor account is not in the selected country
3.2.hint: Choose the country of the bank that holds the debtor account, or pay from an account in the selected country.

3.3.check: Debtor agent BIC country (characters 5–6) matches the selected country
3.3.title: Debtor's bank is not in the selected country
3.3.hint: Choose the country of the debtor's bank, or use the BIC of the bank in the selected country.

3.4.check: All payment blocks belong to the selected country, if CMIplus requires one country per file
3.4.title: Payment blocks of more than one country
3.4.hint: Send one file per country: move the payment blocks of each debtor country into a file of their own.

3.5.check: Payment type can be determined for each transaction
3.5.title: Payment type cannot be determined
3.5.hint: Give the creditor's IBAN, the BIC of the creditor's bank or the creditor's country in the address.

3.6.check: Payment type is supported in the selected country
3.6.title: Payment type not offered in the selected country
3.6.hint: Send this payment as a type the country offers, or choose the country where it is offered.

3.7.check: One payment type per payment block, if CMIplus requires it
3.7.title: Payment block mixes payment types
3.7.hint: Put the payments of each type (for example SEPA and cross-border) into payment blocks of their own.

4.1.title: Message id consists of spaces only
4.1.hint: Give the file a message id (MsgId) of letters and digits, unique for each file.

4.2.check: CreDtTm valid, not in the future beyond a tolerance, not older than the configured number of days
4.2.title: Creation date and time is in the future
4.2.hint: Set CreDtTm to the time the file was created.

age.title: The file is older than allowed
age.hint: Create the file again, or check that an old file is not being sent again. The maximum age is the setting limits.creationDateMaxAge.

4.3.check: NbOfTxs equals the number of transactions in the file
4.3.title: Number of transactions doesn't match
4.3.hint: Set NbOfTxs in the group header to the number of transactions in the file.

4.4.check: CtrlSum equals the sum of all transaction amounts, regardless of currency
4.4.title: Control sum doesn't match the transactions
4.4.hint: Set CtrlSum in the group header to the sum of all transaction amounts.

4.5.check: Initiating party has a name or an identification
4.5.title: Initiating party has no name or identification
4.5.hint: Add the name (InitgPty/Nm) or an identification (InitgPty/Id) of the party that creates the file.

4.6.title: Payment information id consists of spaces only
4.6.hint: Give every payment block a payment information id (PmtInfId) of letters and digits.

4.7.check: Block NbOfTxs, if given, equals the transactions in the block
4.7.title: Number of transactions in the block doesn't match
4.7.hint: Set NbOfTxs of the payment block to the number of its transactions.

4.8.check: Block CtrlSum, if given, equals the sum of the block
4.8.title: Control sum of the block doesn't match
4.8.hint: Set CtrlSum of the payment block to the sum of its amounts.

4.9.check: Payment method is TRF (CHK or TRA only if supported)
4.9.title: Payment method is not TRF

4.10.check: Requested execution date not in the past (or rolled to today, per CMIplus)
4.10.title: Execution date is in the past
4.10.hint: Set the requested execution date to today or a later business day.

4.11.check: Requested execution date not beyond the maximum horizon
4.11.title: Execution date is too far in the future
4.11.hint: Set the requested execution date within the allowed horizon.

4.12.check: In .09, execution date-time (DtTm) used only where supported
4.12.title: Execution date with a time is not supported
4.12.hint: Give the requested execution date as a date only (ReqdExctnDt/Dt), without a time.

4.13.check: Payment type information at block or transaction level, not both
4.13.title: Payment type information on block and transaction
4.13.hint: Give the payment type information (PmtTpInf) either on the payment block or on its transactions, not on both.

4.14.check: Charge bearer at block or transaction level, not both
4.14.title: Charge bearer on block and transaction
4.14.hint: Give the charge bearer (ChrgBr) either on the payment block or on its transactions, not on both.

4.15.title: Debtor name is missing
4.15.hint: Add the debtor's name (Dbtr/Nm) to the payment block.

4.16.check: Debtor account has an IBAN or other ID; account currency, if given, is valid
4.16.title: Debtor account currency is not a valid currency code
4.16.hint: Use an active ISO 4217 currency code for the debtor account (DbtrAcct/Ccy), or leave the currency out.

4.17.check: Debtor agent identified by BIC and/or clearing member ID
4.17.title: Debtor agent has no BIC or clearing member id
4.17.hint: Identify the debtor's bank (DbtrAgt) by its BIC, by a clearing system member id, or both.

4.18.check: Charges account valid; charges account agent is the debtor agent or its branch
4.18.title: Charges account or its agent is not valid
4.18.hint: Use a valid charges account (ChrgsAcct) held at the debtor's bank or one of its branches (ChrgsAcctAgt).

iban.title: Charges account IBAN is not valid
iban.hint: Check the IBAN of the charges account (ChrgsAcct) for typing errors.

account.title: Charges account agent without a charges account
account.hint: Add the charges account (ChrgsAcct), or leave out its agent (ChrgsAcctAgt).

agent.title: Charges account agent is not the debtor's bank
agent.hint: Use a charges account at the debtor's bank (DbtrAgt) or one of its branches; the first 8 characters of the BICs must be the same.

4.19.check: Ultimate debtor, if used, has a name or ID
4.19.title: Ultimate debtor has no name or identification
4.19.hint: Add the name (UltmtDbtr/Nm) or an identification (UltmtDbtr/Id) of the ultimate debtor, or leave the ultimate debtor out.

4.20.check: EndToEndId present and not blank ("NOTPROVIDED" allowed)
4.20.title: End-to-end id consists of spaces only
4.20.hint: Give every transaction an end-to-end id (EndToEndId), or NOTPROVIDED if you have none.

4.21.title: Amount is zero
4.21.hint: Every transaction needs an amount greater than zero.

4.22.check: Decimal places fit the currency (EUR 2, JPY 0, KWD 3)
4.22.title: Too many decimal places for the currency
4.22.hint: Use as many decimal places as the currency has (EUR 2, JPY 0, KWD 3).

4.23.check: Currency is an active ISO 4217 code
4.23.title: Currency is not an active ISO 4217 code
4.23.hint: Use an active ISO 4217 currency code (for example EUR, USD, CZK).

4.24.check: Equivalent amount has a valid currency of transfer and is supported
4.24.title: Equivalent amount is not valid or not supported
4.24.hint: Give the amount as an instructed amount (InstdAmt), or use an active ISO 4217 code as currency of transfer (CcyOfTrf).

currency.title: Currency of transfer is not an active ISO 4217 code
currency.hint: Use an active ISO 4217 currency code as currency of transfer (EqvtAmt/CcyOfTrf).

supported.title: Equivalent amount is not supported
supported.hint: Give the amount in the currency of the transfer as an instructed amount (InstdAmt).

4.25.check: Exchange rate information consistent with the currencies used
4.25.title: Exchange rate information does not fit the transaction
4.25.hint: Check the exchange rate information (XchgRateInf): the unit currency must be a currency of the transaction, and an agreed rate (AGRD) needs the contract id.

unit.title: Unit currency of the exchange rate is not a currency of the transaction
unit.hint: Give the exchange rate for a currency the transaction uses (XchgRateInf/UnitCcy), or leave the unit currency out.

contract.title: Agreed exchange rate without contract id
contract.hint: Add the id of the FX contract (XchgRateInf/CtrctId), or use another rate type.

4.26.check: Creditor agent present where the payment type needs it
4.26.title: Creditor agent is missing for a cross-border payment
4.26.hint: Add the creditor's bank (CdtrAgt), with its BIC or a clearing system member id, name and address.

4.27.check: Clearing system code from the ISO external list and member ID format valid for that system (e.g. USABA 9 digits)
4.27.title: Clearing system code or member id is not valid
4.27.hint: Use a clearing system code of the ISO 20022 list (ClrSysId/Cd) and the member id (MmbId) in the format of that system, for example 9 digits for USABA.

code.title: Clearing system code is not in the ISO list
code.hint: Use a clearing system code of the ISO 20022 list ExternalClearingSystemIdentification1Code (ClrSysId/Cd), or a proprietary one (ClrSysId/Prtry).

member.title: Clearing member id has the wrong format
member.hint: Give the member id (MmbId) in the format of its clearing system, without spaces or separators.

4.29.check: Creditor country is a valid ISO 3166 code
4.29.title: Creditor country is not a valid country code
4.29.hint: Use the ISO 3166 two-letter code of the creditor's country (Cdtr/PstlAdr/Ctry), or XK for Kosovo.

4.30.check: Any postal address is structured or hybrid: TwnNm and Ctry mandatory, max 2 AdrLine, no data repeated between them
4.30.title: Postal address is not a valid structured or hybrid address
4.30.hint: Give the town (TwnNm) and the country (Ctry) in their own elements, at most 2 address lines (AdrLine), and do not repeat structured elements in the address lines.

unstructured.title: Unstructured address is not accepted
unstructured.hint: Give the town (TwnNm) and the country (Ctry) in their own elements; keep at most 2 address lines (AdrLine) for the rest.

missing.title: Town or country of the address is missing
missing.hint: Add the town (TwnNm) and the country (Ctry) to the address.

lines.title: Too many address lines in a hybrid address
lines.hint: Keep at most 2 address lines (AdrLine), or move their content into structured elements (StrtNm, BldgNb, PstCd).

repeat.title: Address line repeats a structured element
repeat.hint: Remove from the address lines (AdrLine) what is already in StrtNm, PstCd or TwnNm.

4.31.check: Creditor account present (except cheques), IBAN or other ID
4.31.title: Creditor account is missing
4.31.hint: Add the creditor's IBAN or account number.

4.32.check: Ultimate creditor, if used, has a name or ID
4.32.title: Ultimate creditor has no name or identification
4.32.hint: Add the name (UltmtCdtr/Nm) or an identification (UltmtCdtr/Id) of the ultimate creditor, or leave the ultimate creditor out.

4.33.check: Instruction codes for agents valid (CHQB, HOLD, PHOB, TELB) and supported
4.33.title: Instruction for the creditor agent is not supported
4.33.hint: Leave out the instruction for the creditor agent (InstrForCdtrAgt/Cd) or use a supported code.

4.34.check: Purpose code in the ISO ExternalPurpose1Code list
4.34.title: Purpose code is not in the ISO list
4.34.hint: Use a purpose code (Purp/Cd) of the ISO 20022 list ExternalPurpose1Code, or leave it out.

4.35.check: Category purpose code in the ISO external list
4.35.title: Category purpose code is not in the ISO list
4.35.hint: Use a category purpose code (CtgyPurp/Cd) of the ISO 20022 list ExternalCategoryPurpose1Code, or leave it out.

4.36.check: Service level code in the ISO external list
4.36.title: Service level code is not in the ISO list
4.36.hint: Use a service level code (SvcLvl/Cd) of the ISO 20022 list ExternalServiceLevel1Code, for example SEPA or URGP.

4.37.check: Local instrument code in the ISO external list or an allowed proprietary value
4.37.title: Local instrument is not in the ISO list or not allowed
4.37.hint: Use a local instrument code (LclInstrm/Cd) of the ISO 20022 list ExternalLocalInstrument1Code, or an allowed proprietary value.

code.title: Local instrument code is not in the ISO list
code.hint: Use a local instrument code (LclInstrm/Cd) of the ISO 20022 list ExternalLocalInstrument1Code, for example INST.

proprietary.title: Proprietary local instrument is not allowed
proprietary.hint: Use a local instrument code of the ISO list (LclInstrm/Cd) instead of a proprietary value (LclInstrm/Prtry), or leave it out.

4.38.check: Remittance: unstructured and structured not combined unless allowed; occurrence limits
4.38.title: Remittance information not as allowed
4.38.hint: Give the remittance information either unstructured (Ustrd) or structured (Strd), within the allowed number of parts.

combined.title: Unstructured and structured remittance information combined
combined.hint: Give the remittance information either unstructured (Ustrd) or structured (Strd), not both.

count.title: Too many remittance information parts
count.hint: Put the remittance information into the allowed number of parts (Ustrd or Strd).

4.39.check: Structured creditor reference type SCOR with valid ISO 11649 RF check digits
4.39.title: Creditor reference RF has wrong check digits
4.39.hint: Check the RF creditor reference (Strd/CdtrRefInf/Ref) for typing errors: it has RF, two check digits and up to 21 letters or digits.

4.40.check: Regulatory reporting indicator and codes valid and allowed
4.40.title: Regulatory reporting is not valid or not supported
4.40.hint: Check the regulatory reporting (RgltryRptg): use an ISO 3166 country code in the details, or leave it out where it is not supported.

country.title: Regulatory reporting country is not a valid country code
country.hint: Use the ISO 3166 two-letter country code in the regulatory reporting details (RgltryRptg/Dtls/Ctry).

5.1.check: Text uses the allowed character set: SEPA Latin set (a–z A–Z 0–9 / - ? : ( ) . , ' + space), SWIFT X set for cross-border, local letters only where CMIplus allows
5.1.title: Characters that aren't allowed
5.1.hint: Replace the characters named in the message. Each payment type has its own character set: SEPA payments the SEPA set, cross-border payments the SWIFT X set, other payments the set of the country.

5.2.check: Characters CMIplus would transliterate (e.g. ä to a)
5.2.title: Characters CMIplus would replace
5.2.hint: Write the characters in their plain Latin form yourself (for example ä as ae or a), so the beneficiary sees what you intend.

5.3.check: No control characters, tabs or line breaks inside values
5.3.title: Control character, tab or line break in a value
5.3.hint: Remove the tabs, line breaks and other control characters from the value.

5.4.check: No leading or trailing spaces, no whitespace-only values
5.4.title: Value starts or ends with a space
5.4.hint: Remove the spaces at the start and the end of the value.

blank.title: Value is only spaces
blank.hint: Fill in the value, or leave the element out if it is optional.

5.5.check: Reference IDs (MsgId, PmtInfId, InstrId, EndToEndId) do not start or end with "/" and contain no "//"
5.5.title: Reference id starts or ends with "/" or contains "//"
5.5.hint: Change the id so that it does not start or end with "/" and does not contain "//".

5.6.check: IBAN country known, length per IBAN registry, mod-97 check digits, national BBAN structure
5.6.title: IBAN is not valid
5.6.hint: Check the IBAN with the account holder. A wrong IBAN can't be corrected safely without them.

dbtr.title: Debtor IBAN is not valid
dbtr.hint: Use the IBAN of your account exactly as the bank gives it.

cdtr.title: Creditor IBAN is not valid
cdtr.hint: Check the IBAN with the creditor. Check digits can't be guessed safely.

5.7.check: BIC is 8 or 11 characters with a valid country code
5.7.title: BIC has an unknown country code
5.7.hint: Check the BIC with the bank: characters 5–6 are the ISO country code of the bank.

5.8.check: Test BIC ("0" as second location character) used in a production file
5.8.title: Test BIC used
5.8.hint: Use the production BIC of the bank. A BIC with 0 as 8th character is a test BIC.

5.10.check: Country codes valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, plus XK where used for Kosovo
5.10.title: Country code is not valid
5.10.hint: Use the ISO 3166 alpha-2 code of the country (XK for Kosovo).

5.11.check: LEI (in .09) has 20 characters and valid ISO 17442 check digits
5.11.title: LEI is not valid
5.11.hint: Check the LEI in the GLEIF database; the last two digits are check digits.

5.12.check: Organisation and private ID scheme codes in the ISO external lists
5.12.title: Unknown id scheme code
5.12.hint: Use a code of the ISO 20022 external code lists, or give the scheme as Prtry instead of Cd.

6.1.check: Elements mandatory in the CMIplus guideline but optional in the XSD
6.1.title: Element required by the CMIplus guideline is missing
6.1.hint: Add the element named in the message.

6.2.check: Elements not supported by CMIplus: forbidden (error) or ignored (warning)
6.2.title: Element not accepted by CMIplus
6.2.hint: Remove the element named in the message.

ignored.title: Element ignored by CMIplus
ignored.hint: CMIplus ignores the element; remove it, or make sure nobody relies on it.

6.3.check: Occurrence limits stricter than the XSD (e.g. 1 Ustrd, 2 AdrLine)
6.3.title: Element occurs more often than the CMIplus guideline allows
6.3.hint: Remove the extra occurrences, or combine their content.

6.4.check: Length limits stricter than the XSD (e.g. names 70, remittance 140)
6.4.title: Text longer than the CMIplus guideline allows
6.4.hint: Shorten the text to the length named in the message.

6.5.check: Maximum payment blocks per file and transactions per file and per block
6.5.title: Too many transactions in the file
6.5.hint: Split the payments into several files.

blocks.title: Too many payment blocks in the file
blocks.hint: Split the payment blocks into several files.

block.title: Too many transactions in the payment block
block.hint: Split the transactions into several payment blocks.

6.6.check: Currency supported for the selected country and payment type
6.6.title: Currency not supported for this payment type
6.6.hint: Use a currency the bank supports for this payment type in the country, or send the payment as another payment type.

6.7.check: Execution date horizon and past-date handling as configured in CMIplus

6.8.check: Batch booking value allowed and its conditions met (e.g. one currency per block)
6.8.title: Batch booking not supported
6.8.hint: Set BtchBookg to false, or leave it out.

currency.title: Batch booking with several currencies
currency.hint: Put the transactions of each currency into their own payment block, or set BtchBookg to false.

6.9.check: Code values within the subset CMIplus supports (purpose, category purpose, service level, local instrument)
6.9.title: Code not supported by CMIplus
6.9.hint: Use one of the codes the bank supports for this field.

purp.title: Purpose code not supported by CMIplus

ctgypurp.title: Category purpose code not supported by CMIplus

svclvl.title: Service level code not supported by CMIplus

lclinstrm.title: Local instrument code not supported by CMIplus

6.10.check: Initiating party identification in the format CMIplus expects
6.10.title: Initiating party id has the wrong format
6.10.hint: Use the initiating party id the bank gave you, in the format of the contract.

6.11.check: Multiple debtor accounts or debtor agents in one file only if allowed
6.11.title: More than one debtor account in the file
6.11.hint: Put the payments of each debtor account into a separate file.

agents.title: More than one debtor bank in the file
agents.hint: Put the payments of each debtor bank into a separate file.

6.12.check: Ultimate debtor and ultimate creditor only where supported
6.12.title: Ultimate debtor not supported for this payment type
6.12.hint: Leave out the ultimate debtor for this payment type.

cdtr.title: Ultimate creditor not supported for this payment type
cdtr.hint: Leave out the ultimate creditor for this payment type.

7.1.title: SEPA payment not in EUR
7.1.hint: A SEPA credit transfer must be in EUR.

7.2.check: Creditor account is an IBAN of a SEPA-scheme country
7.2.title: SEPA creditor account is not an IBAN of a SEPA country
7.2.hint: Give the creditor's IBAN. For an account outside the SEPA countries send a cross-border payment without service level SEPA.

7.3.title: SEPA payment with another service level
7.3.hint: Use service level SEPA for SEPA credit transfers, or leave the service level out.

7.4.title: SEPA charge bearer is not SLEV
7.4.hint: Use charge bearer SLEV for SEPA credit transfers.

implicit.title: A EUR payment within SEPA without service level has another charge bearer than SLEV
implicit.hint: Use charge bearer SLEV, or set the service level to say how the payment should be sent.

7.5.title: SEPA amount outside the limits
7.5.hint: Send an amount within the SEPA limits, or split the payment. The limits are the settings limits.sepaMinAmount and limits.sepaMaxAmount.

7.6.check: Names max 70 characters; remittance one Ustrd of max 140 or one Strd
7.6.title: SEPA name or remittance information too long
7.6.hint: Shorten names to 70 characters and send one remittance part.

name.title: Name longer than 70 characters in a SEPA payment
name.hint: Shorten the name to 70 characters at most.

rmt.title: SEPA remittance information has too many parts
rmt.hint: Send one unstructured remittance line of up to 140 characters, or one structured reference.

7.8.check: Addresses structured or hybrid; unstructured still accepted until the EPC sets a new end date
7.8.title: Unstructured address in a SEPA payment
7.8.hint: Send the address structured: at least town name (TwnNm) and country (Ctry), street and postcode in their own elements.

7.9.check: Debtor address present when the creditor's bank is in a non-EEA SEPA country
7.9.title: Debtor address missing for a creditor's bank outside the EEA
7.9.hint: Add the debtor's postal address (at least town name and country) to the payment block.

7.10.check: Local instrument INST with currency EUR
7.10.title: SEPA Instant payment not in EUR
7.10.hint: Send SEPA Instant payments in EUR, or send the payment without local instrument INST.

7.11.check: Execution date is today, or a future date only if CMIplus supports scheduled instant payments
7.11.title: SEPA Instant payment dated in the future
7.11.hint: Set the requested execution date of SEPA Instant payments to today, or send them as SEPA credit transfers without local instrument INST.

7.12.check: Amount within the configured bank or customer instant limit
7.12.title: SEPA Instant amount above the limit
7.12.hint: Send a smaller amount, or send the payment as a SEPA credit transfer. The limit is the setting limits.instantMaxAmount.

7.13.check: Currency is the local currency of the selected country
7.13.title: Domestic payment not in the local currency
7.13.hint: Send domestic payments in the local currency, or send the payment as a cross-border payment.

7.14.check: Creditor account is a local IBAN or valid local account format (Stage 8)
7.14.title: Domestic payment to an account of another country
7.14.hint: Check the creditor's IBAN: a domestic payment goes to an account in the selected country.

7.15.check: Urgent or standard indicated through service level or local instrument as the local scheme requires
7.15.title: Service level or local instrument not used for domestic payments
7.15.hint: Use a service level and local instrument of the country's domestic scheme (country file, domestic).

7.16.check: Amount above a local high-value threshold sent as standard, where a local rule exists
7.16.title: High-value amount sent as a standard domestic payment
7.16.hint: Check whether the payment must be sent as urgent; the threshold is domestic.highValueThreshold in the country file.

7.17.check: Creditor agent identified by BIC, or by clearing code plus name and address
7.17.title: Creditor's bank of a cross-border payment not identified
7.17.hint: Give the BIC of the creditor's bank, or its clearing member id together with its name and address.

7.18.check: Debtor and creditor addresses structured or hybrid, with TwnNm and Ctry; unstructured still accepted until Swift sets a new date
7.18.title: Unstructured address in a cross-border payment
7.18.hint: Send the debtor and creditor addresses structured or hybrid, with at least town name (TwnNm) and country (Ctry).

missing.title: No postal address in a cross-border payment
missing.hint: Add the postal address of the debtor or creditor, with at least town name (TwnNm) and country (Ctry).

7.19.check: Charge bearer DEBT, SHAR or CRED; SLEV not allowed
7.19.title: Cross-border payment with charge bearer SLEV
7.19.hint: Use SHAR, DEBT or CRED for cross-border payments.

7.20.check: Both banks in the EEA and an EEA currency: SHAR only
7.20.title: Charges not shared between EEA banks
7.20.hint: Use charge bearer SHAR when both banks are in the EEA and the currency is an EEA currency.

7.21.check: Creditor account is an IBAN for IBAN countries, plausible account number otherwise
7.21.title: Creditor account not plausible for the destination
7.21.hint: Give the IBAN for countries that use IBANs; otherwise the account number with letters, digits, spaces, - and / only.

7.22.check: Purpose or regulatory codes required by the destination country (configurable destination list)
7.22.title: Purpose or regulatory reporting missing for the destination
7.22.hint: Add a purpose code (Purp) or regulatory reporting (RgltryRptg) for payments to this country.

7.23.check: Currency plausible for the destination, e.g. BGN is no longer valid for Bulgaria since its euro adoption on 1 January 2026 (https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/bulgaria-adopts-euro-1-january-2026)
7.23.title: Currency no longer in use
7.23.hint: Agree the currency with the creditor; for example Bulgaria uses EUR since 1 January 2026.

7.24.check: Intermediary agent, if given, has a valid BIC
7.24.title: Intermediary bank without BIC
7.24.hint: Identify each intermediary bank (IntrmyAgt1–3) by its BIC, or leave it out.

7.25.check: Text that a downstream format would truncate
7.25.title: Text longer than the cross-border format keeps
7.25.hint: Shorten the text, or expect it to be cut. The lengths are the setting crossBorder.truncateLength.

7.26.check: Creditor account at an RBI bank in the same country: intra-bank transfer rules of the country pack apply
7.26.title: Intra-bank transfer
7.26.hint: No change needed. The country's rules for transfers between accounts at the bank apply.

7.27.check: Budget, tax and customs payments: detected by creditor account or category purpose, checked in Stage 8
7.27.title: Budget or tax payment
7.27.hint: No change needed. Check the country's requirements for budget, tax and customs payments (for example the payer's tax number).

9.1.title: Payment block ID is used more than once
9.1.hint: Give each payment block its own PmtInfId.

9.2.title: Instruction ID is used more than once
9.2.hint: Give each transaction its own InstrId, or leave InstrId out.

9.3.check: EndToEndId unique in the file, except NOTPROVIDED
9.3.title: EndToEndId is used more than once
9.3.hint: Give each transaction its own EndToEndId.

9.4.title: UETR is used more than once
9.4.hint: Give each transaction its own UETR (a new UUID version 4).

9.5.check: Possible duplicate transactions: same creditor account, amount, currency, date and remittance
9.5.title: Possible duplicate payment
9.5.hint: Check whether the payment is in the file twice. If both payments are wanted, make the remittance information differ, for example with the invoice number.

9.6.check: Debtor account equal to creditor account
9.6.title: Debtor and creditor account are the same
9.6.hint: Correct the creditor account: a payment cannot go to the account it is paid from.

9.7.check: Same debtor account in blocks with different debtor names
9.7.title: Same debtor account with different debtor names
9.7.hint: Use the same debtor name (Dbtr/Nm) in every payment block of this account, or check that the account is right.

9.8.check: Same debtor account, date and payment type spread over several blocks
9.8.title: Payment blocks could be combined
9.8.hint: Put payments with the same debtor account, execution date and payment type into one payment block, if nothing else differs between the blocks.

9.10.check: Ultimate debtor identical to the debtor
9.10.title: Ultimate debtor is the debtor
9.10.hint: Leave UltmtDbtr out when you pay for yourself. Give it only for payments on behalf of another party.

10.1.check: Execution date on a weekend or local holiday; CMIplus moves it to the next business day
10.1.title: Execution date is not a business day
10.1.hint: Choose a business day as the requested execution date (ReqdExctnDt), or accept that the payment is executed on the next business day.

10.2.check: Execution date is today and may miss the cut-off (indicative, from configured cut-off times)
10.2.title: Execution today may miss the cut-off time
10.2.hint: Send the file before the cut-off time, or choose a later execution date. The cut-off times shown are indicative.

10.3.check: Text will be truncated by CMIplus or a downstream scheme
10.3.title: Text will be shortened
10.3.hint: Shorten the text to the length shown, so the important part is not cut off.

10.5.check: Elements present but ignored by CMIplus

10.6.check: Recommended data missing: structured creditor address, purpose code, LEI, ultimate debtor for payments on behalf
10.6.title: Recommended data missing
10.6.hint: Add the recommended data shown in the message.

address.title: Structured creditor address recommended
address.hint: Give the creditor address in structured form: StrtNm, BldgNb, PstCd, TwnNm and Ctry.

purpose.title: Purpose code recommended
purpose.hint: Add a purpose code (Purp/Cd) from the ISO 20022 purpose code list.

lei.title: Debtor LEI recommended
lei.hint: Add the LEI of the debtor (Dbtr/Id/OrgId/LEI).

ultimate.title: Ultimate debtor recommended
ultimate.hint: If you pay on behalf of another party, name it as the ultimate debtor (UltmtDbtr).

10.7.check: Hybrid address used where fully structured is recommended
10.7.title: Hybrid address
10.7.hint: Move the information of the address lines (AdrLine) into the structured address elements and leave AdrLine out.

10.8.check: pain.001.001.03 used; migration to .09 recommended if CMIplus plans to retire .03
10.8.title: Older pain.001 version used
10.8.hint: Plan the change to pain.001.001.09. This is a hint only; .03 files are still accepted.

10.9.check: File close to the size or transaction limits
10.9.title: File close to a limit
10.9.hint: Split the payments over more files or payment blocks before the limit is reached.

transactions.title: Close to the limit of transactions per file
transactions.hint: Send the payments in more than one file before the limit is reached.

blocks.title: Close to the limit of payment blocks per file
blocks.hint: Combine payment blocks or send more than one file before the limit is reached.

block.title: Close to the limit of transactions per block
block.hint: Split the payments of this block into more blocks before the limit is reached.

10.10.check: Initiating party differs from debtor; check the ultimate debtor rules for payments on behalf
10.10.title: Initiating party is not the debtor
10.10.hint: Check the bank’s rules for payments on behalf of others: the ultimate debtor (UltmtDbtr) may be needed.

X.1.check: Not in the catalogue yet: EndToEndId NOTPROVIDED
X.1.title: No end-to-end reference
X.1.hint: Send your own EndToEndId so the beneficiary gets a reference.

notImplemented.0.4: Malware scan: not possible in the browser.
notImplemented.0.6: XML declaration and byte-order mark as CMIplus expects: needs the CMIplus expectation.
notImplemented.0.10: Envelope or business application header: needs the CMIplus expectation.
notImplemented.1.5: Namespace prefixes and xsi:schemaLocation as CMIplus accepts: needs the CMIplus expectation.
notImplemented.1.6: Version scheduled for retirement: needs a CMIplus announcement.
notImplemented.5.9: BIC found in the BIC directory: needs the licensed BIC directory.
notImplemented.9.9: MsgId used before by this customer: needs the history of the app.
